question: You declare `List<Course> findByLevl(Level level);` in a repository, with a typo in the property name. When do you find out?
options: When the method is first called in production, as a NullPointerException
Never, because the method returns an empty list
At compile time, because Spring Data generates the code in the build
At application startup, because Spring Data validates the derived query and fails to create the repository
explanation: Derived queries are parsed when the repository is created. A property that does not exist makes the application fail to start, which is much earlier than a failure in production.

question: A screen lists courses with only id, title and level, but the repository returns full Course entities. What is the best change?
options: Return a record such as CourseSummary(Long id, String title, Level level) through a projection method
Mark the other fields as transient in the entity
Cache the entities in a static list
Call entityManager.detach on every entity
explanation: A projection makes the query select only the needed columns and returns plain objects that are not tracked, which is cheaper than loading and dirty-checking entities.

question: A @Modifying update moves every BEGINNER course to INTERMEDIATE. In the same transaction the code then reads an entity it loaded before the update, and it still shows BEGINNER. Why?
options: The update statement failed silently
The bulk update ran in the database but the persistence context kept the old instance
Hibernate rolled back the update at flush
Enums are cached by the JVM
explanation: A modifying query bypasses the persistence context. Using clearAutomatically = true, or reloading the entity, makes later reads see the new value.

question: A search endpoint accepts optional level, title text and minimum lesson count, in any combination. Which approach scales best?
options: One derived method for each combination of parameters
Loading all courses and filtering with streams
Building the JPQL by concatenating the request text
Specifications that each add one predicate and are combined with and
explanation: Specifications turn each optional filter into a small reusable predicate. Combinations multiply derived methods, in-memory filtering loads the table, and concatenation allows injection.

question: Why is `@Query("select c from Course c where c.title = '" + title + "'")` not possible in an annotation, and what is the right way to pass the value?
options: Annotation values must be compile-time constants, so use a named parameter such as :title
Strings cannot contain quotes in annotations, so escape them
Annotations cannot contain JPQL, so use native SQL
The value must be passed through a static field
explanation: An annotation attribute must be a constant expression, so runtime values cannot be concatenated. A named parameter is bound safely by Spring Data and avoids injection.
